correctness.rationale: Assessment of the repaired statement. For smooth a the ten simple branch points give genus four. Directly applying Cartier to y^(-11) x^(j-1) f^5 dx selects exponent 11i-1 and takes eleventh roots, so its square has coefficient product M^(11)M before taking 121st roots. Independent symbolic expansion recovers M. In parity order the two blocks factor as (6a,-C)^t(2a,1) and (C,-6a)^t(1,2a), where C=1-5a^2-3a^4; each has rank one at every parameter, also at a=0. The two blocks of the correctly ordered square have nonvanishing outer factors times opposite scalars ±(2a^11 C-6a)=±5J. Thus the square vanishes on J=0; off it the first image of dimension two is mapped onto itself, and rank stays two. Euclidean division verifies J=a^15-2a^13-4a^11+a is squarefree of degree 15 and J(±2)=∓1. Its gcds with a^2+12 and a(a^2-36) are respectively 1 and a(a^2-36). Under the published equivalence, the exceptional parameters make one orbit; exact modular substitution and pairwise gcds prove each of the remaining twelve roots has six distinct isomorphic parameters, giving two Q8 classes. The a-number two excludes superspeciality. Ran /workspace/repairs/1/verify_frobenius.py (Python 3 and SymPy) successfully, including the counterexample and gcd(J,G)=a(a^2-36).

value.rationale: The standard characteristic-eleven quaternionic family has constant one-step Cartier rank, so its exact rank-zero locus cannot be detected by the superspecial test or by distinguishing one-step ranks. The repaired result identifies precisely two nonsuperspecial geometric curves with p-rank zero and full Q8 in this family, as well as one enhanced class, with a reduced explicit parameter locus. This supplies exact candidates for finer p-torsion or Newton strata and a check against spurious parameter counts, without assuming such finer invariants are determined. It answers the same natural family question as the frozen claim with a substantive, verified replacement.
